atoms.definition: Operation is on the rising edge of clk; active-high asynchronous reset rst clears all message storage, the retained padding region, the result, and DONE, with LANE_COUNT=1 and LAST_BYTECNT=8. Only complete single-block transactions with LANE_COUNT in 1..17 and LAST_BYTECNT in 1..8 are defined; do not write data or configuration during an operation from the START write through DONE; reads and repeated START are allowed. Inputs change after the falling edge and are sampled stably after the rising edge.

atoms.definition: we=1 writes on the rising edge; only the low 8 bits of addr are decoded. 00..87 write 17 64-bit lanes; addr[7:3] selects the lane, bit2 selects the high or low 32 bits, and the low 2 bits are ignored. 88 writes the low 5 bits of LANE_COUNT, and 8C writes the low 4 bits of LAST_BYTECNT; these configurations are not readable. rd=0 or an unmapped read returns 0. When rd=1, 94 returns DONE, and A0/A4/…/BC return the digest from the low 32 bits to the high 32 bits, respectively; the low 2 bits of exact read addresses must be 0. Reads have no side effects, and reads and writes can occur simultaneously.
atoms.title: 32-bit MMIO and address aliasing

atoms.definition: Writing wdata.bit0=1 at 90 generates START with a one-cycle delay; on the next rising edge, the FSM accepts it only when idle or completed, clearing DONE while retaining the old digest; START while busy is ignored and is not queued. The acceptance edge is t0; without an intervening reset, DONE and the new digest update exactly at t0+LANE_COUNT+30 rising edges; DONE holds until the next acceptance or reset. If consecutive START writes span the completion edge, acceptance is determined by the state at that time.
atoms.title: START, completion, and result retention

atoms.definition: The input bytes of each lane are used as message bytes in order from 63:56, 55:48 through 7:0; they map starting at the low byte of the Keccak lane. Only the LAST_BYTECNT high-order bytes of the last lane are taken; when fewer than 8, 06 is placed immediately after the valid bytes and the remaining high-order bytes are cleared; when equal to 8, this implementation does not place an additional 06. The highest bit of lane16 is always set to 1; if the last lane is not 16, lane16 is directly set to 8000000000000000. Lanes lane0..15 not covered by the current message retain their previous padded contents; reset clears them. This history-dependent behavior also applies to shorter subsequent messages; clearing on every operation must not be assumed.
atoms.title: Input byte order and retained padding history

atoms.definition: Set the low 1088 bits of Keccak-f1600 to the 17 padded lanes, with the remaining 512 bits set to 0; the linear index of lane(x,y) is x+5*y. Execute the standard 24 rounds of theta/rho/pi/chi/iota without absorbing the previous state; reverse the bytes within each of the first four output lanes, and arrange lane0 through lane3 from high to low in the 256-bit digest. Keccak uses the standard FIPS202 rotation offsets and round constants. Note that the full-lane padding and retained region described above are the contract of this implementation; the standard SHA3 message API cannot be applied directly to all histories.
atoms.title: Keccak mathematical result and readout order
